title: Prompt Driven Exploration: Language as an Exploration Space for VLA Reinforcement Learning
claim: Sampling varied prompts for a fixed policy and refining them from rollout rewards yields diverse behaviors, without changing policy weights.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right flow, with two feedback loops along the bottom
description: A single left-to-right pipeline diagram. At far left, a rounded box holds the canonical task prompt 'put the green container on the bottom rack'. An arrow leads down to a green 'Prompt Sampler' box showing ρ(·|g) and a neural-network icon. Gray arrows fan out to three lavender candidate-prompt boxes, with ellipsis dots between them. Each prompt is a paraphrase or variant, such as one that adds 'completely'. The prompts feed into a tall cyan 'Policy' block with a π symbol and a robot icon. Each prompt then produces a row of three robot-manipulation video frames labeled Trajectory τ. At the far right, a green check, a red cross and a green check show the reward for each trajectory. Two long return arrows run along the bottom: a blue 'RL Update' arrow back to the policy and a green 'Prompt Refinement' arrow back to the sampler. Section titles are color-coded: purple, blue and green.
caption: Prompt changes elicit different behaviors from the same policy. (a) Nearby trajectories of the same color show action-noise rollouts under a fixed prompt; different colors show modes induced by different prompts. (b) Adding "completely" to the placement instruction turns failure into success without updating policy weights.
abstract: Exploration is essential to reinforcement learning (RL) since a policy cannot improve by repeatedly sampling the behaviors it already prefers. Standard methods inject stochasticity in the action space, but such jitter only yields rollouts close to the original action distribution. Escaping a weak policy often requires global perturbations that action noise cannot produce. Large language models (LLMs) and vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a pathway: they condition the policy on a natural language prompt, and since the rollout follows from it, modifying the prompt induces global changes. The challenge is finding prompts that induce useful global changes. With a weak policy that rarely succeeds, reward is too sparse to select on. Our idea is to refine prompts from the rollouts themselves: a vision-language model (VLM) reasons over the rollout video, diagnoses how the policy responded, and rewrites the prompt to elicit better behavior next time. Sampling a prompt and holding it fixed throughout a rollout provides episode-level commitment, analogous to posterior-sampling exploration. We call this strategy Prompt Driven Exploration (PDE). Across manipulation and reasoning tasks, PDE enables RL to learn successful policies even from zero-reward starts, and improves sample efficiency more broadly. Our website is available at https://xinyunsunshine.github.io/prompt-rl.
